name: Limiting privacy risks while learning
gist: Building learning algorithms that extract insights from data while mathematically guaranteeing that sensitive information about individuals remains protected.
explain: A hospital wants to train a model to diagnose disease using patient records. But patient data is sensitive: names, addresses, medical histories, genetic information could be misused if leaked or stolen. The hospital faces a dilemma: the more data they use, the better the model, but more data means more privacy risk and more potential harm if the model is compromised. Additionally, even if the data is properly secured, a clever adversary might extract sensitive information about specific patients from the model's predictions — just by seeing how the model responds. A technique called membership testing can determine whether a specific patient's data was in the training set by observing how the model behaves, which reveals private facts without accessing the database. This subtheme tackles: how can you learn useful models while mathematically guaranteeing that sensitive information remains private?

The challenge is that perfect learning and perfect privacy seem to conflict. A model trained to fit data well might memorize specific individuals' sensitive attributes. In distributed settings where data stays on individual devices and only model updates are shared, an adversary might infer private information from the updates. Additionally, privacy has multiple faces: differential privacy protects individual records, but other concerns include inference privacy (preventing attackers from deducing properties of the training set), and fairness privacy (preventing models from using sensitive attributes like race). Standard privacy techniques like data anonymization are brittle — they fail when multiple datasets are combined or linked.

Researchers develop differential privacy, a mathematical framework that adds controlled noise to computations or data, ensuring that an adversary cannot confidently infer whether any single individual's data was in the training set, even with infinite computing power. They analyze privacy-utility tradeoffs: how much accuracy you lose to gain privacy protection, so practitioners can choose the right balance for their setting. They study federated learning, where models are trained on data that never leaves individual devices, combining local models with privacy guarantees, which keeps sensitive data on each person's phone or device. They investigate privacy-preserving inference: once a model is trained, how should you deploy it to prevent extraction of sensitive training data from model queries? They also examine when privacy protection must come early (adding noise during training) versus late (limiting what queries to the model are allowed), because timing affects how much noise is needed. The work aims to enable beneficial learning from sensitive data without exposing individuals, which protects vulnerable populations from harm and from being re-identified or targeted — a risk that exists even with strong data security because the model itself can leak — while allowing the data to be useful for improving care or diagnosis so society benefits from the data without sacrificing privacy.

papers.title: Barriers to Counterfactual Credit Attribution for Autoregressive Models
papers.contribution: Establishes theoretical barriers showing CCA autoregressive models face significant challenges unlike differential privacy approaches.

papers.title: Differentially Private Continual Release with Relative Error
papers.contribution: The work shows error can be substantially reduced via relative terms under non-adaptive streams while proving adaptive streams admit unavoidable large error for selection tasks.

papers.title: Differentially Private Equilibrium Finding in Polymatrix Games
papers.contribution: First algorithm achieving vanishing Nash gap and privacy budget simultaneously as players increase, with numerical validation.

papers.title: Memorization Through the Lens of Sample Gradients
papers.contribution: CSG achieves five orders of magnitude efficiency gain over exact memorization scores and enables early stopping at weight norm peak without validation set.

papers.title: Understanding Private Learning From Feature Perspective
papers.contribution: Shows private signal learning requires higher SNR than non-private, and proves that noise memorization in non-private learning transfers to private learning, reducing generalization.

papers.title: A Statistical Framework for Analyzing Specification Resistance to Learnware-Inversion Risks
papers.contribution: First framework analyzing specification privacy risk in learnware, proving that properly-sized RKME specifications introduce negligible privacy risk while retaining sufficient identification information.

papers.title: Adaptively Robust Resettable Streaming
papers.contribution: We achieve polylogarithmic space complexity supporting (sub)linear statistics including L_p moments and Bernstein statistics with prefix-max error guarantees.

papers.title: Dataset Distillation for Memorized Data: Soft Labels can Leak Held-Out Teacher Knowledge
papers.contribution: Shows that students can achieve non-trivial accuracy on held-out memorized data, demonstrating a privacy vulnerability in knowledge distillation.

papers.title: Differentially Private Two-Stage Gradient Descent for Instrumental Variable Regression
papers.contribution: First work providing both privacy guarantees and provable convergence rates for instrumental variable regression in linear models with precise accuracy-privacy trade-off bounds.

papers.title: Keeping a Secret Requires a Good Memory: Unconditional Streaming Lower-Bounds for Differentially Private Algorithms
papers.contribution: Proves that any private algorithm for distinct-element estimation requires almost Ω(T^{1/3}) space, establishing the first exponential separation between private and non-private space complexity for this task.

papers.title: Optimal Domain-Aware Privacy Mechanisms for Synthetic Data Generation
papers.contribution: PubMix significantly improves synthetic data quality compared to domain-agnostic privacy mechanisms.

papers.title: Optimal conversion from Rényi Differential Privacy to $f$-Differential Privacy
papers.contribution: Establish that the intersection rule achieves optimal bounds uniformly for all RDP profiles and Type I error levels, marking the fundamental limit of what can be inferred from RDP guarantees alone.

papers.title: Optimization, Generalization and Differential Privacy Bounds for Gradient Descent on Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
papers.contribution: Show polylogarithmic width suffices for 1/T optimization and 1/n generalization; identify qualitative gap between non-private and private training regimes revealing polylogarithmic width necessity.

papers.title: Privacy-Aware Data Integration for Enhanced Quantile Inference under Heterogeneity
papers.contribution: Establishes consistency, normality, and effectiveness with rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrates robust inference across heterogeneous scenarios.

papers.title: Unlearning Evaluation through Subset Statistical Independence
papers.contribution: The method provides a simple, standalone evaluation procedure that reliably distinguishes in-training from out-of-training subsets and differentiates unlearning effectiveness.
